input.question: What tensions between helpfulness and harmlessness do RLHF-trained assistants show, and how have researchers tried to reduce them?

supporting.quote: There is a tension between helpfulness and harmlessness, which can be measured at the level of both preference modeling and RLHF-trained policies
supporting.why: Helpfulness and harmlessness are in tension.

supporting.quote: An AI assistant that answers all questions with “I don’t know” would be harmless, but of course it would also be completely useless
supporting.why: Constitutional AI aims for harmless but non-evasive answers.

supporting.quote: This is an example of an “alignment tax” since our alignment procedure comes at the cost of lower performance on certain tasks
supporting.why: Alignment can cost performance on some tasks.

draft_answer: Training for helpfulness can make models harmful and vice versa; Constitutional AI aims for harmless but non-evasive answers, and RLHF can impose an alignment tax.
